title: Characteristic polynomial of an idempotent endomorphism over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $n\ge0$, $V=k^{\oplus n}$ and $p:V\to V$ a $k$-linear map with $p\circ p=p$. Let $r=\dim_k\operatorname{Im}(p)$. Then the characteristic polynomial of $p$ [def-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module] (computed in any basis [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module-properties]) is $\det(T-p)=(T-1)^rT^{n-r}\in k[T]$. In particular it divides $T^n(T-1)^n$ in $k[T]$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M5 (lemma-lift-projective-module, line 2020): 'For every prime p containing I the image of f in kappa(p) is (x-1)^r x^{n-r} where r is the dimension of P-bar (x) kappa(p)' (stated without proof)

proof.text: The idempotent image decomposition gives $V=\operatorname{Im}(p)\oplus\operatorname{Im}(1-p)=\operatorname{Im}(p)\oplus\ker(p)$, by [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-endomorphism-image-base-change] specialized to the field $k$. On $\operatorname{Im}(p)$ the map $p$ is the identity, since $p(pv)=pv$, while on $\ker(p)$ it is zero. The range and kernel are finite-dimensional subspaces. Their dimensions satisfy $r+\dim_k\ker(p)=n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly-rank-nullity], so $\dim_k\ker(p)=n-r$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M5 (lemma-lift-projective-module, line 2020), the image of an idempotent and its complementary summand; the restriction identities are immediate from p^2=p

proof.text: Choose bases of the two finite-dimensional summands and concatenate them. In this basis $p$ is the direct sum of the identity on $\operatorname{Im}(p)$ and the zero map on $\ker(p)$. Basis invariance from [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module-properties] and the direct-sum formula [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-direct-sum-free] therefore give $\det(T-p)=\chi(1_{\operatorname{Im}(p)})\,\chi(0_{\ker(p)})$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M5 (lemma-lift-projective-module, line 2020), the characteristic polynomial of the fibre idempotent in a basis adapted to its image

proof.text: Apply the identity and zero characteristic-polynomial leaves [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly-identity] and [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly-zero] to the two summands. Their dimensions are $r$ and $n-r$, hence $\chi(1_{\operatorname{Im}(p)})=(T-1)^r$ and $\chi(0_{\ker(p)})=T^{n-r}$. Multiplying yields $\det(T-p)=(T-1)^rT^{n-r}$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M5 (lemma-lift-projective-module, line 2020), the displayed fibre characteristic polynomial

proof.text: Since $0\le r\le n$, the factors have exponents bounded by $n$: $(T-1)^r$ divides $(T-1)^n$ and $T^{n-r}$ divides $T^n$. Thus their product divides $T^n(T-1)^n$ in $k[T]$.

lean.statement: theorem charpoly_toMatrix_of_idempotent {k : Type u} [Field k] (n : ℕ) (p : Module.End k (Fin n → k)) (hp : IsIdempotentElem p) (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) k (Fin n → k)) : let r := Module.finrank k (LinearMap.range p) (LinearMap.toMatrix b b p).charpoly = (Polynomial.X - 1) ^ r * Polynomial.X ^ (n - r) ∧ (LinearMap.toMatrix b b p).charpoly ∣ (Polynomial.X : Polynomial k) ^ n * (Polynomial.X - 1) ^ n
